rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Seeking His bounty” is coordinated with “your sleep,” so the signs include sleeping at night and seeking sustenance by day.
rows.anchor: The verse would thus mean: among His signs is the night in which you sleep and the day in which you strive

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi notes that earlier sūrahs contain parallels to this interpretation of night and day.
rows.anchor: Parallels of this interpretation can be seen in earlier sūrahs.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Listening ranks below reflection and knowledge but remains a means of guidance: sensible people can learn by attending to what sensible people say.
rows.anchor: it is lesser in status than the two above mentioned faculties, yet it is also a means of acquiring knowledge.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing appeal to listeners sarcastically criticizes opponents whose hostility keeps them from hearing and benefiting from the Qurʾān and the Messenger’s arguments.
rows.anchor: This sentence is a sarcastic critique on the attitude of the opponents that those who are bent upon animosity instead of

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lightning evokes hope and despair, anticipation and fear: it commonly heralds rain, but can also bring destruction to a nation.
rows.anchor: lightning which has the aspects of hope and despair as well as of anticipation and fear in it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān recounts destructive lightning striking ʿĀd and Thamūd; Islahi says he explained its implication at the relevant places.
rows.anchor: in the destruction of the ‘Ād and the Thamūd and I have explained its implication at relevant places.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because mercy and destruction both lie with God, people should turn to Him in hope and fear; assigning mercy and punishment to separate deities is wrong.
rows.anchor: both mercy and destruction are in the hands of God. For this reason in the states of hope and despair as well as

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second sign is that God directly governs the universe and, under His just law, rewards or punishes nations.
rows.anchor: the fact is that He is directly running these affairs and according to His law of justice rewards or punishes nations.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third sign is that God needs no separate agent to punish a nation; He can turn any blessing into a bane.
rows.anchor: He does not need a separate team for this task; He can turn any of his blessings into a bane.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revival of dead earth by rain reprises an argument Islahi discussed while explaining verse 19.
rows.anchor: while explaining verse 19 earlier.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intact heavens and earth answer the imagined objection that such a secure system could not be shattered at the Resurrection; Arabs similarly asked who could move the mountains and dismissed the Day as a bluff.
rows.anchor: they regarded the threats of the advent of this Day to be mere bluff.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens and earth persist only by God’s command and for as long as He wills; He can destroy that system and replace it without difficulty.
rows.anchor: the heavens and the earth are intact because of God’s behest and shall remain intact as long as He wants them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will call people from the earth once and they will immediately emerge; He will not need to repeat the call.
rows.anchor: He will just need to call people once from the earth and everyone will immediately issue forth.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi cites al-Inshiqāq 84:2 to illustrate the created order obeying its Lord’s command.
rows.anchor: and obeys its Lord’s command and this only is befitting for it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything in the heavens and earth belongs to God as His obedient creature, so nothing can disobey or deviate from His call.
rows.anchor: whatever the heavens and the earth contain are His creatures and are subservient and obedient to Him alone.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse about originating and recreating creation confirms the preceding promise of resurrection and introduces the coming theme of monotheism.
rows.anchor: also encapsulates the topic of monotheism which is coming up.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rationale for resurrection given here was also stated earlier in verse 11.
rows.anchor: This rationale of being raised up on the Day of Judgement has also been given in verse 11 earlier.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If people accept God created them, they should not find recreation improbable: they should consider whether creating initially or repeating creation is harder.
rows.anchor: when the addressees of this verse accept that it is He who has created them, why do they regard His recreating them to be improbable?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the phrase about the most exalted attribute, mathal means an attribute.
rows.anchor: the word لَثَمۡال connotes an attribute.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurʾānic language uses familiar human words for divine attributes so people can gauge them, while intending meanings fitting the Almighty’s transcendence.
rows.anchor: without adopting it, these attributes cannot be properly gauged by us; obviously, they have been used in the higher meaning which befits the Almighty.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone merits every noble attribute in heaven and earth; no one shares them, so no one can be His peer in the duties owed to Him.
rows.anchor: It is said that it is He who is worthy of all noble attributes found in the heavens and the earth.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is mighty and wise: He dominates all things, His works embody wisdom, and nothing can impede His intention except His wisdom.
rows.anchor: He is dominant on everything and is exalted and that all His works are based on wisdom.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse refutes associating others with God by asking people to use their own social dealings as a proof: would they give servants equal shares in wealth God gave them or treat them like relatives?
rows.anchor: God presents their own mutual dealing as a proof of His claim. They are posed this question: Do they regard their slaves and servants to have an equal share

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word khawf here means “to give regard”; Islahi says it has a range of senses discussed elsewhere in his commentary.
rows.anchor: The word وفًخ here means to “give regard.” It is used in wide meanings

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People who deny equal ownership to their own servants nevertheless assign partners rights belonging to God, an unjust psychological inconsistency since God alone merits those rights.
rows.anchor: when these people are not ready to grant their slaves equal ownership to what they have even though it has been given to them by God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi compares this argument with the Qurʾānic criticism of polytheists who ascribe daughters to God while disliking daughters for themselves and feeling ashamed of them.
rows.anchor: the polytheists ascribe daughters to God while they themselves dislike daughters and even feel ashamed to let others people know

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beyond signs in human nature, the surrounding world, nature, and intellect, polytheists are challenged for ascribing to God what they dislike for themselves; they should be even stricter about it on God’s behalf.
rows.anchor: notwithstanding the fact that there are plenty of arguments and signs against polytheism in the world inside man and that around him as well as in nature and intellect

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument has completed its objective, and the verse’s ending says these arguments benefit those who use their intellect, not those who have neglected it.
rows.anchor: For those who do not use their intellect and have consigned it to oblivion, these arguments can be of no avail.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Those who have done wrong” refers to polytheists, whose association of partners with God is a grave act of injustice.
rows.anchor: refers to the polytheists who are guilty of committing an oppression as great as polytheism.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “without knowledge,” knowledge means argument and proof; the wrongdoers follow desires and innovations blindly instead of following evidence.
rows.anchor: the word ٍمۡلِع connotes “argument and proof.” In other words, it is not knowledge and proof which they have made their guide

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although God gave people intellect, those who surrender to whim are allowed to wander under God’s law, and such people cannot be guided by anyone.
rows.anchor: God has blessed human beings with intellect but many wretched people have consigned their reins to their whims.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those led astray persist in wandering through life: they have no helper in this world to return them to the path or in the Hereafter to save them from destruction.
rows.anchor: neither is there anyone for them in this world who can bring them back to the right path nor will they find any helper in the Hereafter

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Section III (30–39) follows the answer about the Romans’ defeat by the Persians: it calls the Prophet and companions to Islam, prayer, and giving, then warns Quraysh of imminent accountability and promises blessing to adherents of Abraham’s religion.
rows.anchor: Now in the succeeding verses, the Prophet (sws) and his companions are strongly urged to follow with full concentration and devotion the religion of nature

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular address is plainly to the Prophet, but he is addressed as Muslim leader and advocate; the following verses use plural address and plural circumstantial accusatives.
rows.anchor: the address is in the singular which is an obvious indication that it is directed to the Prophet (sws). Yet this address to him is in his capacity of the leader

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet and companions should devote themselves to God’s true religion and disregard their opponents, whose objections have already been shown baseless.
rows.anchor: The Prophet (sws) and his companions should devote themselves to the true religion of God and just ignore their opponents.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-dīn is Islam, the true religion preached by all prophets and completed through Muhammad; Islahi cites 3:19 as declaring Islam the only true religion in God’s sight.
rows.anchor: The word ُنۡیِّالد refers to the true religion of God: Islam. It was this religion to which all prophets and messengers of God called their people

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥanīf means devoted and dedicated; its Qurʾānic association with Abraham recalls his example of dedication to monotheism.
rows.anchor: The word فۡیِنَح means “devoted and dedicated.” The implication is that while disregarding all the filth of polytheism

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A verb is elided in the phrase about God’s primordial nature, supplied from the preceding verb: turn away from all else and follow the nature on which God created people.
rows.anchor: Here a verb is suppressed which is evident from the previous verb. The implication would be: “while disconnecting yourself from everything follow this religion of nature
